newsitem.title: SPAIN: Heavy rain and snow grip Spain, four dead.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rain and snow grip Spain, four dead.

text.p: Heavy snow and rain on Wednesday claimed four more lives in Spain, cutting off hundreds of communities and blocking many roads.

Agricultural associations said damage to crops had worsened since the first spate of bad weather in December. Farmers' association ASAJA put the damage to crops in southern Spain so far at around 150 billion pesetas ($1.13 billion).
In the region of the Bajo Guadalquivir alone, 10,000 hectares (25,000 acres) of cultivated land remained flooded, the association added.
In the south, one of the worst-hit areas, flooding caused by torrential rains washed through fields, villages and towns.
Police said that in the Andalusia region a person drowned in a bloated river while another was swept away while fishing alone. A couple died when their house collapsed.

Heavy snow engulfed highland areas and civil defence officials said 251 communities had been completely isolated. More than 7,000 people were affected, mostly in the region of Asturias and the provinces of Burgos, Lerida and Zamora.
Snow also blanketed the northern and central provinces of Galicia, Madrid, Castilla y Leon and Cataluna.
Traffic organisations said 240 roads had been blocked by rain and snow throughout the country.
Although temperatures are forecast to rise and rain and snow expected to ease, a return to normality is expected to take some time.
